To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
higher educational attainment was associated, on average, with lower body mass index at age 20 and lower increase in body mass index up to recruitment.
higher education is associated with lower BMI in early adulthood and lower weight gain during adult life, and that this is particularly the case for men.
higher educational attainment was associated both with a lower BMI at age 20 and a lower increase of BMI until age at recruitment, but with a lower increase in body weight during follow-up.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between education and weight change in the European Proscentive Investigation into Cancer and nutrition.
the relationship between socioeconomic status (SES) and health.
the role that education and educational attainment play in relation to the development of overweight and obesity in adulthood.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
higher education is associated with lower weight change in adult life.
higher educational attainment is related to lower body mass index in adulthood.
the higher educated have lower weight gain during adult life than the lower educated, but that they are still gaining weight, and thus are not immune from the obesity epidemic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

higher educational attainment was associated to a lower BMI at age 20 and a lower increase of BMI up to recruitment, but during follow-up after the first measurement, a gain in body weight was seen in all educational levels.
higher educated individuals are more likely to have a healthy body weight at age 30 years and are less likely to gain weight during adult life.
the association of education with obesity risk is stronger at the start of adulthood than at the end.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the association between education and body weight change over time is not linear and that the relationship between higher education and lower body weight change is not limited to the early stages of adulthood.
the association of education with weight change is complex and may be influenced by a combination of factors.
the association between education and body weight is not static and should be interpreted in the context of the life course.
